full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J: The accused petitioner, Abdur Rahman, obtained this Rule on 4-2-2001, under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, calling upon the informant opposite party No. 1 Shankar Sen Gupta and the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, to show cause as to the legality and propriety of the proceeding in Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000 corresponding to GR Case No. 190 of 2000, pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, against the accused petitioner under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code. At the time of issuance of the Rule all further proceeding in GR Case No. 190 of 2000, pending as aforesaid, has been stayed by this Court. 

 2. One Shankar Sen Gupta lodged a petition of complaint before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, against the accused petitioner, Abdur Rahman, as accused No.2 and one Abul Kalam Azad as accused No.1, alleging that the accused petitioner committed offence under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code and the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, sent the said petition of complaint to the Kotwali Police Station, Chittagong, for treating the same as FIR. Thereupon, Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3) 2000 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code has been started against the accused petitioner upon the said petition of complaint which, there- after, has been registered as GR Case No. 190 of 2000 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 3. The police commenced investigation in Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000 and upon finding the guilt of the accused persons, prima facie, submitted charge sheet against the accused persons under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code prior to which the accused petitioner Abdur Rahman who is the accused No.2 in the first information report, voluntarily surrendered before the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong and obtained enlargement on bail. Thereafter, the accused petitioner, Abdur Rahman, alone preferred this miscellaneous application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 5. Mr Bashiruddin Zindigir, at the very outset, has taken us through the entire assertion made in the first information report of the Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000, Annexure-A, and strenuously argued that the alleged Bainapatra dated 18-8-1996 has been the subject matter of a suit for Specific Performance of Contract pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong being Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998, filed by the accused No.1, Abul Kalam Azad, the father-in-law of the accused petitioner, Abdur Rahman and, as such, the private complaint as lodged by the complainant opposite party No. 2 claiming the Bainapatra as false is barred under the provision of section 195(1)( c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Mr Zindigir while confronted with the established principle of law that no defence materials could be considered at the stage of proceeding under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, argued that since the complainant opposite party No.1 categorically mentioned the date of the alleged forged Bainapatra and since the affidavit-in opposition filed by the complainant opposite party No.1 categorically admitted the existence of such a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, the necessary relation in between the statement in the petition of complaint and the defence material has been established and, as such, the Bainapatra which is the subject matter of the suit for specific performance of contract became the part of the prosecution material and, as such, this court is entitled to look into the said part of the prosecution material in order to make finding as to the maintainability of the Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000. Mr Zindigir further submits, that since the accused petitioner submitted the original copy of the Bainapatra dated 18-8-1996 in the civil Court and since the original Bainapatra, against which the allegation of forgery has been raised before the criminal Court, the instant proceeding in GR Case No. 190 of 2000 is an abuse of the process of the court. Mr Zindigir prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 6. On the other hand, the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Md Afsar Hossain, in opposing the Rule, submits that the Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000 involved not only section 471 but also involved sections 420, 467 and 468 of the Penal Code which is not scheduled offence under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the said Criminal Proceeding, so far it relates to the offence committed under sections 420/467/468 of the Penal Code, is not barred to proceed against the accused petitioner. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further argues that the statement made in the counter-affidavit submitted by the complainant opposite party No.2 shows that the schedule, as mentioned in the Bainapatra dated 18- 8-1996, and the schedule mentioned in the plaint of the Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998 not being the same, the instant proceeding in GR Case No. 190 of 2000 cannot be termed as an abuse of the process of the court. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, prays for discharge of the Rule. 

 8. It appears from the first information report, Annexure-A appended to the miscellaneous application, that the informant raised allegation against the accused petitioner, Abdur Rahman and his father-in-law Abul Kalam Azad that they have created the alleged forged Bainapatra dated 18-8-1996 and thereby committed the offences under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code and therefore, the complainant initiated the private proceeding in Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, against the accused persons. It appears from Annexure-D, appended to the miscellaneous application, that the accused No. 1 of Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000, AbuI Kalam Azad filed a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, being Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998, in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong, against the informant Shankar Sen Gupta and Dibakar Sen Gupta as defendants praying for Specific Performance of Contract dated 18-8-1996. It further appears from Annexure-D(2), which is the certified copy of the firisti form related to filing of some documents in Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998, pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong, that it contained an endorsement that the Bainapatra dated 18-8-1996, in its original copy, has been filed before the said court. Mr Bashiruddin Zindigir indicating this state of affairs that the complainant opposite party No.2 admitted the filing of the suit for Specific Performance of Contract, being Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998, argued that the necessary relation in between the statements in the first information report and the Annexure-D and Annexure-D(2) has been established. We find sufficient force in the argument of Mr Zindigir. A defence material could be turned into a part of prosecution material if it is admitted by the prosecution in any manner or a bridge could be shown to have been established in between the materials, either on the admitted facts or in any other manner. Since the alleged Bainapatra admittedly is in the seisin of a civil Court, which fact has also been admitted in the affidavit-in-opposition submitted by the complainant opposite party No.2 in the proceeding, the plaint submitted in the Other Class Suit No. 49 of 1998 has become a part of the prosecution material of the Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000 and, as such, the court is entitled to look into it for coming to a finding as to the legality and propriety of the proceeding. 

 9. It appears that section 195(1)( c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides a bar against initiation of private complaint on the allegation of forgery of a document which is the subject matter of a suit or case in any civil, criminal or revenue Court. Section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is reproduced below; 

 10. In the case of Md Tokumuddin Par vs State reported in 4 BLT(AD) 84 their Lordships in the Appellate Division on the self-same question held as under; 

 "section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that in case where the alleged forged deeds have been produced or given in evidence in any Court the institution of the Criminal case is barred on the basis of a private complaint." 

 11. But in the case before us a question has arisen, as the learned Deputy Attorney-General argued, that a Criminal Proceeding initiated upon private complaint against commission of offence under not only section 471 but also under sections 467/468 and 420 of the Penal Code whether sustainable in view of the prohibition made under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the ground that the alleged forged document has been produced in evidence in a proceeding before any Civil, Criminal or Revenue Court. The question being of vital importance we have examined the different provisions of law and also the decisions of the apex Court on the point. 

 12. In that case Nur Ahmed vs Kalimuddin reported in 1987 BCR (AD) 152 their Lordship in the Appellate Division while deciding the question held as under: 

 22. This proposition has support from the decision as taken by their Lordship in the Appellate Division in the case of Abdul Hai Khan vs State and another reported in 40 DLR (AD) 226. In that case the accused appellant No.1 had filed Title Suit NoA10 of 1975 renumbered as Title Suit No.1 of 1979, in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khu1na, against defendant Ashutosh Debnath for specific performance of a contract for sale of a land on the strength of a Bainapatra dated 15 July, 1971 executed in his favour by the owner, the said Ashutosh. The suit was, however, dismissed on merit by a judgment dated 15 September 1980 with the observation that the Bainapatra produced by the plaintiff was a forged document. Thereupon, the owner's bargader Md Ziad Ali Khan, who is respondent No.2 in this appeal, lodged a complaint on 21 May 1982 before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Khulna, alleging that the Bainapatra had been forged by the plaintiff of the suit who also produced it in court as evidence, and on that complaint cognisance was taken by the Magistrate and process was issued against the plaintiff and four others who had participated in the forgery all of whom are appellants here under section 467, 468 and 471 of the Penal Code. The appellants challenged the proceeding against them by an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure taking the ground that the cognisance as taken on a private complaint was totally barred by section 195(1)( c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure in that when the alleged forged document was produced in evidence in court it was the court alone which was competent to make a complaint. 

 23. In course of argument in that case, the learned Additional Attorney-General, opposing the appeal, submitted that at least the offence tinder section 467 of the Penal Code stands outside the ambit of the prohibition of section 195 and that cognisance of this offence on private complaint is perfectly lawful. In reply to this submission his Lordship, Mr Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed, CJ, as his Lordship was then, after examining different decisions of Indian and our Jurisdiction, specially the case of Raja Xushal Pal Singh, AIR 1931 All 443, State of Gujarat vs Bhikubhai, AIR 1965 Gujarat 70 and the Indian Supreme Court decision arrived at in the case of Patal Laljibhai, AIR 1971 SC 1935 came to the finding in paragraph No. 15 that both the offences, forgery and use of forged document, are closely linked with one another and, as such, these offences clearly fall very much within the ambit of section 195(c). 

 26. At a later stage in the case of Mrs Shahar Banoo Ziwar Sultan Beyed vs Mrs Wahida Khatoon and another reported in 1996 BLT (AD) 154. his Lordship Mr Justice ATM Afzal, as his Lordship was then, on the similar question held unambiguously in the following terms: 

 27. In view of the above provision of law and the decision of the apex court we are of the opinion that since the alleged forged document has been filed in the civil Court which is the subject matter of a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, it is for the concerned civil Court to lodge any complaint before the criminal Court if it finds the forgery relating to the said document. But since the instant proceeding in GR Case No. 190 of 2000 under sections 420/467/468/471 has been initiated on private complaint the same cannot continue in view of the provision of section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the proceeding now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, as GR Case No. 190 of 2000, under sections 420/467/468/471 is found to be an abuse of the process of the court and is liable to be interfered with by this court in its inherent jurisdiction. 

 30. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The proceeding in GR Case No. 190 of2000 arising out of Kotwali Police Station Case No. 29(3)2000, under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, now pending before the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, is hereby quashed.
